newsitem.title: NORWAY: BP stays mum on deepwater Nyk oil results.
newsitem.headline: BP stays mum on deepwater Nyk oil results.

text.p: British Petroleum Norge said on Friday it was still too early to speculate on any hydrocarbon discoveries in the frontier Nyk High area in the Norwegian Sea following the spudding of the first deepwater well on the Norwegian continental shelf.
The company was responding to speculation in the Norwegian media that BP's first exploration well had failed to encounter oil and had found small quantities of gas.

"It's too early for us to make a confirmation and we have no comment on media speculation," BP spokesman Jan Erik Geirmo told Reuters. "We are talking to the Oil Directorate (OD) about when information on the drilling can be released. We hope to have something next week."
The OD is charged with releasing any results of drilling in Norwegian waters.
On May 28 BP said it had encountered a reservoir and taken a sample from well 6707/10-1, which was drilled in a water depth of 1,270 metres.
BP plans to drill through the reservoir down to a total depth of about 5,000 metres below sea level.
On Thursday the daily financial Dagens Naeringsliv said the Nyk well had encountered "enormous quantities of water but no oil".

"As already known the people of northern Norway have more than enough water as it is, and there is no reason to be happy about the fact that BP so far in the drilling programme, has found gas reserves of approximately 100 million cubic metres," DN said.
BP, in partnership with Saga Petroleum ASA, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS and Esso, was awarded the Nykhoegda deepwater licence PL218 in Norway's 15th licensing round last year.
